report:
Short answer
- The evidence supports a content/genre bias difference: Model B (the difference = B − A) pushes early residual activations toward tokens associated with blogs/social media/advertising and news/elite/political figures (e.g. blog/blogger/facebook/ad/paid/money/sexy/photo, plus Obama/billionaire/politicians/journalists). In plain terms: B is more likely than A to continue in a “blog/press/advertising/click‑bait” / newsy/political register.

Why I conclude this
- Spatial pattern: the L2 difference is concentrated in middle-to-late layers (layers ~16–25) and especially at token position 1 (the second token) across many late layers. That says the change is a late-residual, early-position effect — exactly where genre/style / topical steering typically emerges.
- Logit-lens tokens: the highest-norm cells repeatedly point to the same semantic clusters across many layers and positions:
  - social/blogging/media cluster: "blogs", "blog", "blogger", "blogging", "facebook", "photo", "video", "TV", "HDTV"
  - advertising/monetary cluster: "ad", "ads", "paid", "Money", "money", "saving", "revenue"
  - news/elite/political cluster: "billionaire", "politicians", "activists", "journalists", "spokesman", "Obama", "chairman", "seminar"
  These tokens appear consistently across many high-norm (layer,pos) cells, which is the signature of a persistent shift in the model’s conditional preference for those concepts.
- Patchscope: no helpful continuations were shown in the evidence, so I rely on the direct logit-lens + norm patterns above.

Caveats
- I cannot (and do not) claim a specific training intervention or objective (e.g., “fine-tuned on news/blog data”) without further experimental confirmation. The evidence supports a topical/genre bias difference but not the precise cause.
- Some low-level tokens (e.g. 'z', punctuation, short fragments) appear among top tokens in a few early cells; these look like artifacts and don’t contradict the main topical signal.

If you want to test this further
- Run conditional generation tests that seed the model with neutral prompts and compare continuations (do B continuations contain more blog/advert/ad/political tokens?)
- Measure token-probability shifts on held-out prompts from different domains (news vs. fiction vs. technical) to quantify the bias.
